config.noncreatureaffinity.option.maxAff: Numeric cap, default 100; no separate behavior or token stage. Familiar ≤ Close ≤ Close friend ≤ cap; lower-stage thresholds above the next boundary are reduced.
config.noncreatureaffinity.option.minAff: Lower bound of affinity. Negative values allow a creature to dislike the player.
config.noncreatureaffinity.option.initia: Initial affinity when a relation is created. Zero is first meeting and preserves original behavior; stage behavior starts at positive affinity.
config.noncreatureaffinity.option.friend: Intimate and maximum-affinity stages are merged. Default 75. Completed interactions with positive settlement gains award a token at this threshold; close-friend trade eligibility uses it too.
config.noncreatureaffinity.option.affini: Affinity gained after one completed mating animation.
Extra affinity when the player started the mating themselves.
Affinity lost when rejecting a friendly creature request.
Extra affinity lost when you break out of a FORCED mating, on top of the rejection penalty. Set to 0 and breaking free only forfeits that mating's reward.
config.noncreatureaffinity.option.nonStr: Use NeedsOfNature's struggle screen for forced matings

When on, a forced mating is started as a NeedsOfNature mob attack, so its own A/D mash bar and real escape progress appear. The costs (all existing NeedsOfNature behaviour): escaping can hurt you, grants its brief invulnerability, counts towards its escape statistics, the creature may come after you again, and its Give Up chain becomes active; if NeedsOfNature's destroyed-skin feature is on, you also accumulate destroyed-skin damage when the animation starts. When off, only this module's break-free key can end it, at the same affinity cost.
config.noncreatureaffinity.option.affini: Affinity lost per in-game day without interaction. 0 disables decay.
config.noncreatureaffinity.option.autoTa: Tame tameable creatures automatically once they become friends.
config.noncreatureaffinity.option.tameOw: Bind tamed ownership to the player who reached the threshold.
config.noncreatureaffinity.option.friend: Enable automatic defense: creatures at the familiar threshold use their existing combat abilities to help an attacked player. Vanilla pets and creatures with companion controls currently unlocked follow their own rules, independently of this toggle.
Radius around the defending creature for finding targets that recently attacked the player.
Reserved. Not applied yet: changing damage would conflict with NeedsOfNature.
config.noncreatureaffinity.option.reques: Arousal a friendly creature needs before asking for mating.
Legacy compatibility only. Requests use the configured familiar threshold.
How often (in ticks) creatures consider asking. 20 ticks is about one second.
Probability per check that a request is issued (0 to 1).
Maximum distance at which a creature will ask.
Time to answer: default 30 seconds, minimum 1. Timing out costs affinity; moving beyond 16 blocks still cancels immediately.

Cooldown for requests converted from NoN autonomous starts: default 15 seconds, minimum 0. Scoped to this player and creature; does not restrict manual or native direct interactions. Managed by the server owner.
config.noncreatureaffinity.option.forceM: Rejecting a request triggers one forced mating.
config.noncreatureaffinity.option.forced: You can still break free from a forced mating by attacking.
Reserved. Forced mating currently starts immediately.
config.noncreatureaffinity.option.offspr: Applies to inferred nearby same-species parents, not confirmed fathers. Auto-friend uses the threshold instead. NoN player birth supplies no father entity, so this setting does not apply there.
New offspring only. On: start at the friendship threshold. Off: NoN player-born offspring use initial affinity. Existing offspring and NoN auto-taming are unchanged.
Offspring generation is parent generation plus one.
How far a newborn looks for its parent.

config.noncreatureaffinity.option.compan: Wait radius (blocks)
In WAIT mode a companion further than this from the ordered spot is walked back to it. The creature is not frozen and can still defend itself in place.
Combat fact memory (ticks)

How long a recorded attack stays usable as a reason to engage. Short-lived facts are what allow a fight to START; an established fight is re-checked on its own terms and does not end when the fact expires.
Give up after no progress (ticks)
How long a companion may fail to close on its target, and land no hit, before the chase is abandoned. Closing distance or landing a hit both count as progress, so a long melee is never cut short.
Stalled target off limits (ticks)
After a chase is abandoned for lack of progress, the target stays off limits for this long. Without it the next hostility scan walks the companion straight back into the same unreachable fight.
Recalled target off limits (ticks)
After a recall, how long the enemy left behind stays off limits. This is what stops the recall/charge-back/re-recall loop.
Return window after a recall (ticks)
How long a recalled companion keeps returning before it answers anything new. A companion already back beside you is exempt, so a real threat next to it is still answered immediately.
